what_it_does: Modern chip design requires characterization of timing (how fast signals propagate) across thousands of operating conditions—temperature, voltage, process variations. Running SPICE simulation (the standard circuit simulator) for every combination is too slow. This work treats timing characterization as a generative modeling problem: train a hybrid GAN-autoencoder on a sample of simulations to learn the distribution of timing behaviors, then generate realistic timing data for untested corners without simulation. The result: accurate timing libraries at a fraction of the simulation cost.
